questions.question: Explain how you would develop the chosen sketch of the rescue device into fixed sizes, and justify your choice of pivot position.
questions.expected_answer: Measure the parts that cannot change first, the syringes, about 110 millimetres long with a 70 millimetre plunger travel, and size the base to hold the syringe and arms, for example 300 by 120 millimetres of doubled card, which fits the A4 constraint. Make the arms 200 by 25 doubled card so they reach forward and do not bend. Choose the pivot position from the mechanical advantage needed: 60 millimetres from the jaw tip and 140 from the back gives a grip force more than double the push but a smaller opening, about 30 millimetres; moving it to 80 from the tip opens wider but grips less. Record the choice and the reason, and if a specification is missed, revise it openly or adjust the design.

questions.question: Describe the steps for producing the oblique drawing of the device and explain why the side is chosen as the front face.
questions.expected_answer: On squared paper at 1 to 2, draw feint construction lines for the base, syringe, pivot block, two crossed arms, rod and saddles in the side view, check proportions, then draw depth lines from each visible corner back at 45 degrees along the grid diagonals, all equal and about half the real width, join the ends for the back edges, darken the visible outlines, leave construction lines feint, and label every part with a title, name, date and scale. The side is chosen because the arms, pivot, syringe and jaws are all visible there in true shape and the round pin and holes remain true circles.

questions.question: State what the working drawing of one view must contain so that a classmate could build the device, and list four items from the parts list.
questions.expected_answer: One view at a stated scale, with every real size in millimetres dimensioned once on thin dimension lines with arrowheads and extension lines: base 300 by 120, arms 200 by 25 with centre lines, pivot hole 6 diameter located 60 from the jaw tip, rod holes located from the ends, block and saddles located from the edges, hidden edges dashed where needed. Beside it a parts list with part, quantity, material and size, for example base 1 double corrugated card 300 by 120; arm 2 double card 200 by 25; rod 1 straw 90 long; split pins 4; plus two syringes and one metre of tubing.
